toc.title: Levers for Services, Storage and Scheduling
More Key Terms in One Line

html:
1What You Will Learn

  • Match each component to its job, and each need to its object
  • Recall the levers for Services, storage and scheduling
  • Name the CNCF projects and what each one does
  • Translate old names and key terms at a glance

2Cluster Components and Their Jobs

  • Control plane: kube-apiserver is the front door; etcd keeps the state; kube-scheduler places Pods; kube-controller-manager runs the controllers
  • cloud-controller-manager connects the cluster to a cloud provider
  • Node: the kubelet runs Pods, kube-proxy sets up Service rules, and the container runtime runs containers
  • Everything talks to the API server, and only the API server talks to etcd

Exam tip

Everything goes through the API server; only it talks to etcd.

3Which Object Do I Use?

I need to Use
run a stateless app with rolling updates Deployment
give each Pod a stable name and its own storage StatefulSet
run one Pod on every node DaemonSet
run a task to completion, or on a schedule Job, CronJob
keep settings out of the image; keep a secret value ConfigMap, Secret
give Pods a stable address inside the cluster Service
route HTTP from outside by host and path Ingress or Gateway API
ask for persistent storage PersistentVolumeClaim
limit what a namespace can use ResourceQuota
Exam tip

Name the need first, then the object that fits.

4Levers for Services, Storage and Scheduling

  • Services: ClusterIP inside only; NodePort a port on every node; LoadBalancer an external balancer; ExternalName an alias; headless no virtual IP
  • Storage: emptyDir lives with the Pod; PV is the storage, PVC the request; RWO per node, RWOP per Pod; Retain keeps data, Delete removes it
  • Scheduling: selectors and affinity attract; taints repel; tolerations permit; HPA adds Pods, VPA resizes them, Cluster Autoscaler adds nodes

Exam tip

Attract, repel, spread, scale: name the lever's direction.

5Security Layers and Controls

  • Request path: authentication, then authorization with RBAC, then admission
  • Admission: mutating first, then validating; Pod Security levels are Privileged, Baseline and Restricted
  • The workload: a securityContext, a NetworkPolicy and a ServiceAccount with only the access it needs
  • Supply chain: scan, sign, use a private registry, verify at admission
  • Phases: develop, distribute, deploy, runtime; older material says the 4 Cs

Exam tip

Who, what may they do, is the object acceptable, how does it run, where did it come from.

6Probes, Release Strategies and Signals

Topic Quick answer
Liveness probe a failure restarts the container
Readiness probe a failure removes the Pod from the Service endpoints
Startup probe protects a slow starter from the liveness probe
Recreate, rolling, blue/green stop all then start; replace gradually; switch whole environments
Canary, A/B, shadow a share of traffic; chosen users; a copy of each request
Metrics, logs, traces numbers over time; messages; the path of one request
Exam tip

Readiness controls traffic; liveness controls restarts.

7CNCF Projects and Their Jobs

  • Runtime: containerd and CRI-O through the CRI; runc starts containers
  • Networking: Cilium, Calico and Flannel are network plugins; CoreDNS is cluster DNS; Istio and Linkerd are service meshes
  • Delivery: Argo CD and Flux are GitOps agents; Helm packages charts; Argo Rollouts does progressive delivery; Kustomize patches YAML
  • Observability: Prometheus pulls metrics; OpenTelemetry generates telemetry; Jaeger traces; Fluent Bit and Fluentd collect logs

Exam tip

Learn each project by its one-line job.

8More Projects and Their Jobs

Area Projects and their job
Cluster data etcd: the key-value store behind the API
Storage Rook: orchestrates Ceph for file, block and object storage
Scaling KEDA: event-driven autoscaling
Security and policy Falco detects odd runtime behavior; OPA Gatekeeper and Kyverno enforce policy; Cosign signs and Trivy scans images
Platform Crossplane: control planes for infrastructure; Backstage: developer portal; Knative and OpenFaaS: serverless
Events and cost CloudEvents: a common event format; OpenCost: spend visibility
Load balancing MetalLB: LoadBalancer Services on bare metal
Exam tip

Match the job to the project, not the other way round.

9Old and New NamesOld wording]** **[Moving

Older name or fact Now
PodSecurityPolicy removed: Pod Security admission replaces it
dockershim removed: nodes need a CRI runtime such as containerd or CRI-O
Endpoints API deprecated: EndpointSlices
Ingress frozen: Gateway API is the successor
The 4 Cs the lifecycle phases: develop, distribute, deploy, runtime
Five domains, 46/22/16/8/8 four domains, 44/28/16/12
  • As of 30 October 2026: the Ingress NGINX controller is retired, so it is not a safe choice for new designs
Exam tip

Map an old name to its new home and answer the same way.

10Key Terms in One Line

Term One line
Pod the smallest deployable unit: containers that share network and storage
Namespace a way to divide a cluster; the scope for names and quotas
Label and selector key-value tags, and the queries that connect objects
CRD and operator a new API kind, and a controller that manages an application
Taint and toleration repel, and permit
Sidecar a helper container in the same Pod
Drift the actual state moving away from the desired state
SLI, SLO, SLA a measurement, a target, a contract
Immutable infrastructure replace rather than change
Idempotent the same result when repeated
Exam tip

If a term is new in a question, find it in this table first.

11More Key Terms in One Line

Term One line
Controller a loop that compares the actual state with the desired state, and acts
Reconciliation the repeated act of moving the actual state toward the desired state
Requests and limits what a container reserves for placement, and the most it may use
Ingress controller the program that applies the rules of Ingress objects
PV and PVC a piece of storage, and the request for it
RBAC roles and bindings that decide who may do what in the API
Admission controller a step that can change or reject an object before it is stored
GitOps Git holds the desired state, and an agent keeps the cluster in line
Error budget the share of failures that the SLO allows
Exam tip

The glossary file of this module lists many more terms.

12Quick Reference Card

Topic Key fact
Components the API server in the middle, etcd behind it, scheduler and controllers beside it, kubelet and proxy on nodes
Objects match the need to Deployment, StatefulSet, DaemonSet, Job, Service, Ingress, PVC or ResourceQuota
Levers Service types, storage modes and scheduling levers, each with a direction
Security and delivery request path, Pod Security, supply chain; probes and release strategies
Projects and names one-line jobs for the projects, and old names mapped to new ones
